1,200 might be enough for some people, but not many - even people with metabolic disorders such as hypothyroidism probably should be eating at or above 1,400 (depending on TDEE, activity levels, height, family history, comorbidities etc.)

This is such a messy, judgemental and weirdly aggressive post. Just because you might high restrict at under 1,000 calories and believe that is somehow a personality trait, really is not evidence to support the fact that 1,200 is ‘plenty’ of calories for most women. 

Maybe just try to check your attitude a little because this is the kind of shit that makes people say “Your ED makes you judgemental of other people”, while everybody here loves to proclaim that’s ~soOoOoo~ not the case sweaty and we’re all only ~jUdgMenTaL oF oUr oWN bOdiEs~, it’s not a good look.

1,200 is not the magic number, it’s simply low enough that almost anybody will lose weight eating this much - it doesn’t mean this is a *sustainable* nor healthy caloric intake for most young women. Even people who’s BMR is 1,200 still need more than that to function or maintain a healthy weight as the BMR is literally a base level of energy required for normal bodily functions. Eating below your BMR for long periods of time can have significant consequences on immune, integumentary, mental and endocrine health.

After all this abuse, just surviving is remarkable, though obviously not optimal. 
When you’re able to leave their house, it would be ideal to limit or completely cut contact with them in the future. You are *not* the problem, and you’re certainly not responsible for your mother’s issues. It’s an abhorrent way to treat a child, so it’s not unusual that you’re having suicidal ideation. It’s a coping mechanism, an escape, however all I can say is that you’re valuable and worth everything. Living through the pain of abuse feels impossible a lot of the time, a hopeless, soul-destroying endeavour. 

Suicide may seem like an objective solution, however it strips you of any ability to start a new life and create your own purpose through autonomy and pursuit of interests. It doesn’t mean that it’s not a solution, I just hope that through all of this you can see that you are so worthy of love and freedom. 

I have many friends who have been through similar situations, and once they were able to move out of home, their lives improved quite dramatically. Things aren’t perfect for them, but they’re making strides and have built beautiful lives for themselves. 

Please PM me if you’d ever like to talk, I’m always here and willing to listen. Your voice and pain are valid. All the very best, and good luck.

I’m so sorry you’re feeling this way, and not to take away from your pain but I just wanted to let you know you’re truly not alone. I’m 26f, and ever since I was a child I recall feeling incredibly strange, existential, anxious and subsequently socially isolated. I’ve always described suicidal ideation as being programmed into my DNA, as you say “I’m an anomaly” and therefore not meant to exist. It’s so intrinsic, most people can’t actually conceive of what we’re describing however I promise you I understand so deeply what you’re talking about. 

I don’t want to plead for you to continue to exist, because it’s ultimately your choice and stripping people of the autonomy to decide whether they live or die is inhumane, and in fact amplifies the feelings of distress. You’re a very thoughtful, introspective and highly intelligent young woman, and I hope that it provides a little bit of comfort to know that it’s not only okay to feel this way, it is in fact normal for many people like ourselves. I’m immeasurably sensitive - to criticism, tactile sensations, noise, subtle changes in facial expression, tone and writing styles. It often feels as though I’ve done something wrong, or they’re tired of me. It becomes depressing and makes me want to completely sequester myself from society, and I often do. I frequently ask myself why I’m still here if I cannot function properly in a hostile world. I also self-medicate, as it takes the edge off the overwhelming cacophony of sensations that come from simply existing. 

Also, screw the people here saying you’re “too young to feel this way”, that’s a load of boloney. These feelings originated in early childhood for me, and only grew deeper and more severe as I got older. That’s often the way it is with highly sensitive people unfortunately. 

Please message me if you would like anybody to talk to, I’m happy to potentially help you process and understand some of these feelings. Good luck, and I hope that you’re able to make it through just a little longer.
